data_fields.name: alternative_chance
data_fields.donor_constant: default 1.0 per blueprint alternative; 0.5 and 0.1 in cactus data

data_fields.name: nothing_alternative
data_fields.donor_constant: blueprint id null = place nothing; weight via chance (flower data: 0.5)

data_fields.name: child_slots
data_fields.donor_constant: named slots per kit, each maps to one child kit id (saguaro: 3 slots)

data_fields.name: max_recursion_depth
data_fields.donor_constant: no cap in donor (placeSbb has no depth argument); sketch uses 8

data_fields.name: horizontal_child_turns
data_fields.donor_constant: fixed 0 turns for horizontal child slots

data_fields.name: root_column_width
data_fields.donor_constant: 32 tiles per root column (roots picked by index mod count)

best_idea: A hub is a kit with named service slots and a weighted list of base layouts (including nothing), and each slot is filled by its own child kit, so a town block is composed from data one slot at a time.
decision_why: Take the slot-and-child kit grammar and the weighted nothing alternative; add the depth cap the donor lacks; reject the voxel paste, the column stripes and the sign text, which do not fit Frankendom's zones.
acceptance: A server test with a fixed seed builds a hub with three named service slots and asserts each configured slot holds at most one child kit; a kit with a 0.5 nothing alternative is empty about half the time over 1000 seeds; a cyclic kit reference stops at the depth cap without error.
